fruity_sweet.quote: "count on this oriental being a fruity, syrupy experience"
fruity_sweet.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
fruity_sweet.reason: The Guide's whole description is of a fruit-punch, syrupy smell, while the opening is tagged only saffron and jasmine.

vanilla_gourmand.quote: "sweetened by an outrageous amount of ca. 3% of ethyl maltol"
vanilla_gourmand.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
vanilla_gourmand.reason: Scent and Chemistry says the Ambroxan core is sweetened with about 3% ethyl maltol (cooked sugar) and the Guide calls it syrupy, yet no stage carries the sugar family.

vanilla_gourmand.quote: "counterbalanced by an even more extreme amount of ethyl maltol"
vanilla_gourmand.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
vanilla_gourmand.reason: The ethyl maltol dose is described as a structural part of the main accord, so the sugar should persist beside the Ambroxan in the drydown.

woody_amber.quote: "the kind that smells like rubbing alcohol played at heavy metal concert volume"
woody_amber.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
woody_amber.reason: The Guide describes the woody-amber as loud enough to cover the rest of the composition, so it belongs in the heart as well.

woody_amber.quote: "a huge dose of some vile woody-amber material"
woody_amber.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
woody_amber.reason: The Guide says a very large dose of a woody-amber aromachemical dominates the scent, but the drydown tags it at 0.3 under resinous amber.

coffee_gourmand.quote: "The huge chocolate-mothballs-cucumber accord of Black Orchid was a clever idea"
coffee_gourmand.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
coffee_gourmand.reason: The Guide names chocolate as the first element of Black Orchid's defining accord, but no stage carries the cacao family.

iris_powdery.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
iris_powdery.reason: The Guide makes iris the note that defines the scent and calls it a linear wall-of-sound perfume, but the entry drops iris entirely after the heart.

cedar_dry.quote: "25% of 6.92 / 6.93 already in the earlier woody-violet-leaves creation 'Fahrenheit'"
cedar_dry.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
cedar_dry.reason: Scent and Chemistry reports 25% Iso E Super (compound 6.92/6.93), a long-lasting material the drydown does not carry at all.

vanilla_gourmand.quote: "one in the heart (some sort of gourmand accord)"
vanilla_gourmand.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
vanilla_gourmand.reason: The Guide places a gourmand accord in the heart, where the entry has none (sweetness starts only in the drydown).

white_musk.quote: "in front of a musk‐ (39%) and Iso E Super"
white_musk.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
white_musk.reason: The chemistry book gives the base as 39% musk, the largest share it names, yet the drydown carries no musk tag.

cedar_dry.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
cedar_dry.reason: The same passage gives 15% Iso E Super in the base, which this site files under dry cedar / Iso E Super.

vanilla_gourmand.quote: "feels, right from the start, like an old drydown"
vanilla_gourmand.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
vanilla_gourmand.reason: The Guide says the vanilla drydown character is there from the first spray, while the opening is tagged only citrus, saffron and spice.

cedar_dry.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
cedar_dry.reason: The Guide names cedarwood as one of the two main materials, but the drydown has no cedar tag.

citrus_fresh.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
citrus_fresh.reason: Chemistry says Bourdon doubled the dose of dihydromyrcenol in Cool Water and describes that material as citrusy and lime-like; the Guide calls this style not-quite-citrus.

cedar_dry.quote: "declaring his love for Iso E Super ( 1.45 , ca . 35%)"
cedar_dry.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
cedar_dry.reason: Chemistry gives about 35% Iso E Super, a dose that is present from the heart onward, yet the heart has no cedar tag.

cedar_dry.quote: "5% of Texas cedarwood oil in the Jean‐Claude Ellena 's woody milestone"
cedar_dry.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
cedar_dry.reason: With 35% Iso E Super plus 5% cedarwood oil, cedar should lead the drydown rather than sit below vetiver.

tobacco_honey.quote: "with tobacco and woody notes letting us know that Sì has suave male company"
tobacco_honey.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
tobacco_honey.reason: The Guide hears tobacco with the woods in the background of the development; no stage carries a tobacco tag.

vanilla_gourmand.quote: "an unearthly large amber-toffee chord, then dissolves in coughing fits"
vanilla_gourmand.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
vanilla_gourmand.reason: The Guide says the first minutes are a large amber-toffee chord, while the opening is tagged citrus, white floral and aquatic only.

oud_smoky.quote: "And I’m sorry, was there supposed to be oud?"
oud_smoky.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
oud_smoky.reason: The reviewer smelled no oud at all, so oud should not be a leading heart family.

vanilla_gourmand.quote: "an almond biscuit gourmand and a fruity green rose"
vanilla_gourmand.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
vanilla_gourmand.reason: The review names a biscuit gourmand as one of the two halves of the scent, which the heart tags omit.

oud_smoky.quote: "And I’m sorry, was there supposed to be oud?"
oud_smoky.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
oud_smoky.reason: Same review: no perceptible oud, so the drydown should not present oud as a main family.

fruity_sweet.quote: "count on this oriental being a fruity, syrupy experience"
fruity_sweet.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
fruity_sweet.reason: The Guide describes the whole wear as fruity and syrupy, but fruit is tagged only in the opening.

vanilla_gourmand.quote: "sweetened by an outrageous amount of ca . 3% of ethyl maltol"
vanilla_gourmand.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
vanilla_gourmand.reason: Ethyl maltol at about 3% is a candy-sugar overdose, so the sugar family belongs among the main drydown families.

rose.quote: "a few masculine scents with dominant rose themes"
rose.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
rose.reason: The chemistry book lists it among masculines with a dominant rose theme, but rose is tagged only in the opening.

patchouli.quote: "Exactly the same content of 19.5% patchouli oil is also present"
patchouli.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
patchouli.reason: The chemistry book gives 19.5% patchouli oil in Black Aoud, an overdose that makes patchouli a leading base family.

iris_powdery.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
iris_powdery.reason: The Guide names violet and musk as the whole character, so violet should lead the heart rather than trail white florals.

aldehydes.quote: "Byredo’s take on the aldehydic floral, somewhere between No.22 (Chanel) and White Linen"
aldehydes.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
aldehydes.reason: The Guide classes it as an aldehydic floral like No. 22 and White Linen, where aldehydes carry past the opening.

cedar_dry.quote: "a dry sandalwood scent accented with cedar"
cedar_dry.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
cedar_dry.reason: The chemistry book gives 7.5% Texas cedarwood oil and describes the scent as sandalwood accented with cedar, but cedar vanishes from the drydown tags.

fruity_sweet.quote: "This is a solid if unexciting peachy floral"
fruity_sweet.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
fruity_sweet.reason: The Guide hears a peach floral, while the heart is tagged as pure white floral with no fruit.

sandalwood_creamy.quote: "some nutty-lactonic-woody blur borrowed from Gucci Rush (1999)"
sandalwood_creamy.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
sandalwood_creamy.reason: The Guide describes a lactonic woody drydown, which matches the milky-wood family rather than dry cedar alone.

iris_powdery.quote: "several intense ingredients in overdose: cinnamon, orris, vanillin"
iris_powdery.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
iris_powdery.reason: The chemistry book lists orris among the overdosed materials, and the tags have no iris at any stage.

animalic.quote: "an excessively rich, sweet, and animalic floral oriental"
animalic.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
animalic.reason: Both sources put animalic notes at the centre of the scent, so animalic should rank with vanilla in the drydown.

fruity_sweet.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
fruity_sweet.reason: The Guide describes a woody-fruity rose, and the heart has no fruit tag.

cedar_dry.quote: "‘ Black Afgano ’ ( Nasomatto , 2009) with 6% of Texas cedarwood oil"
cedar_dry.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
cedar_dry.reason: The chemistry book gives 6% Texas cedarwood oil, a large dose, and cedar is untagged.

white_musk.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
white_musk.reason: The reviewer found it muskier than Cetalox alone, but musk is tagged only faintly in the drydown.

sandalwood_creamy.quote: features already 3.7% of natural sandalwood oil
sandalwood_creamy.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
sandalwood_creamy.reason: The Chemistry book reports 3.7% natural sandalwood oil, a base material that lasts into the drydown, where the entry has no sandalwood.

sandalwood_creamy.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
sandalwood_creamy.reason: The Guide labels it "not sandalwood" and finds only one synthetic sandalwood molecule, so sandalwood should not read as the lead heart family.

oud_smoky.quote: equal parts of Cool Water and any one of the lamentable so-called ouds
oud_smoky.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
oud_smoky.reason: The review describes half the scent as a Western-style synthetic oud accord, but the heart carries no oud.

tobacco_honey.quote: it ends up merely like a not very interesting pipe tobacco
tobacco_honey.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
tobacco_honey.reason: The review says the scent ends as pipe tobacco, but the drydown has no tobacco tag.

coffee_gourmand.quote: chocolate-patchouli was memorably achieved by Chris Sheldrake twice
coffee_gourmand.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
coffee_gourmand.reason: The Guide names Coromandel (with Lutens Borneo 1834) as one of two landmark chocolate-patchouli scents, so cacao is a co-lead with patchouli rather than a minor accent.

woody_amber.quote: We find previously unimaginable levels of 13.6% of 8.127 in 'Bois d'Argent'
woody_amber.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
woody_amber.reason: At 13.6% Ambrox is a high-impact, radiant material that is already evident by the heart, not only in the base.

woody_amber.quote: We find previously unimaginable levels of 13.6% of 8.127 in 'Bois d'Argent'
woody_amber.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
woody_amber.reason: Compound 8.127 is (-)-Ambrox; the book calls 13.6% an unprecedented dose, yet the entry has no woody amber at any stage.

patchouli.quote: The subtle and gentle orris-honey-patchouli-incense theme of 'Bois d'Argent Cologne'
patchouli.source: Ohloff, Pickenhagen, Kraft and Grau, Scent and Chemistry (2022)
patchouli.reason: The book names patchouli as one of the four themes of the scent; the entry has no patchouli.

green_herbal.quote: turn tuberose into a herbal note
green_herbal.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
green_herbal.reason: The review says the ginger and aromatics turn the tuberose herbal, but the heart is tagged as white floral only.

spicy_warm.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
spicy_warm.reason: The Guide classes the scent as "ginger tuberose", so ginger runs through the heart rather than only the opening.

tonka_coumarin.source: Turin and Sanchez, Perfumes: The Guide 2018
tonka_coumarin.reason: The review describes sweet hay and calls the result a fougere, and a second review describes Twilly as tuberose in a "coumarin context"; the entry has no tonka.
